prior_findings.assessment: Current source and durable P-4b artifacts still prove synchronous quiescence/reset boundaries, two non-vacuous overlap runs, ordered cancellation, and no post-reset leakage.

The strict task-to-replacement-canvas identity assertion remains intact. The durable negative control still removes only the identity guard, fails on the intended stale r1 assertion, restores byte-identically, and passes after restoration.
The in-repository negative-control harness and raw log remain directly inspectable and prove bounded execution, attribution, fail-safe restoration, and a restored positive rerun.

Durable gate artifacts remain present and current. Package evidence directly proves installed-binary launch plus worker/cMap/font GET byte equality and HEAD status, empty body, and matching content-type/content-length/cache-control headers.

Theme application itself is repaired: data-theme is applied after navigation, computed dark/light palettes genuinely differ, and every dark/light PNG pair has a different hash. However, direct visual inspection shows both light rail captures have blank PDF canvases, unlike their dark counterparts. The harness waits for a nonblank canvas before changing theme; the theme change can trigger viewer relayout/rerender, but it performs no post-theme nonblank assertion before capture. Thus the eight-cell matrix remains partially vacuous.

gate-package.log now safely omits config-root filenames, per-file config metadata, paths, and secret-derived hashes while retaining complete in-memory Bun.deepEquals snapshot comparison and installed-asset proof. However, the supposedly privacy-safe durable review set still explicitly records the sensitive config filename in the gate index and transaction receipts, and the source diagnostic comment also embeds it. This contradicts the round-6 requirement that durable output contain no sensitive user-config filename.

blocking_findings.finding: The two light-theme rail cells are visually vacuous as PDF-rendering evidence: their page canvases are blank, while the corresponding dark captures visibly contain the Viewer Link Fixture text. The harness calls waitForNonBlankCanvas before applying data-theme, then captures without rechecking after the theme-induced relayout/rerender. Distinct hashes and settled theme variables therefore do not establish eight real, rendered cells.
blocking_findings.required_fix: After applying and settling each theme, wait again for the current visible canvas to contain nonblank pixels and assert the expected rendered-page/text subject before taking the rail screenshot. Regenerate the full eight-cell matrix and visual-theme-proof.json; retain the existing theme-difference, pair-hash, and overview-subject assertions.

blocking_findings.finding: Although gate-package.log no longer emits sensitive config details, durable artifacts and the diagnostic source comment still name the credential-bearing user-config file explicitly. The requested privacy property forbids retaining its filename as well as its path/hash/stat metadata. The gate index's claim that the verifier was purged repo-wide is therefore incomplete with respect to the filename prohibition.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Replace the concrete credential filename everywhere in durable artifacts and diagnostic comments with a generic phrase such as "credential-bearing config file." Preserve the privacy-safe aggregate output, installed-package asset hashes, and the unchanged full in-memory snapshot equality assertion. Re-run a repository-wide check demonstrating that neither the sensitive filename nor the prior secret-derived verifier remains.
